title: HYPOChLorous Acid TEsting Studies: Interventional DRAINAGE
summary: Hypoclates:Drainage investigates whether continuous irrigation of interventionally placed percutaneous irrigation drainages with hypochlorous acid (HOCl, Granudacyn®) is more effective compared to episodic irrigation with isotonic saline solution in the treatment of fluid collections and abscesses in the abdominal cavity or pelvis. Percutaneous irrigation drainages are routinely used to achieve more efficient wound cleansing and faster healing through irrigation of the inflamed area. The study aims to evaluate the therapeutic benefit of HOCl-based continuous irrigation, primarily assessed by the drainage dwell time and duration of antibiotic therapy. Additionally, the duration of hospital and intensive care unit stays after drainage placement as well as inflammatory markers over time are considered. The results could help optimize future therapy recommendations based on evidence. Furthermore, this is one of the first studies to examine the efficacy of HOCl as an active agent in interventional drainage therapy in an actual clinical context.
conditions: Infection following a procedure, not elsewhere classified

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of clinical routine data from approximately 150 patients who underwent interventional percutaneous placement of an irrigation drainage (episodic irrigation with isotonic NaCl solution) in the period September-November 2025.

Prospective analysis of clinical routine data from approximately 150 patients undergoing interventional percutaneous placement of an irrigation drainage, defined by irrigation with Granudacyn® at 1000 ml per 24 hours for at least 3 days, in the period September 2025 to February 2026.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who underwent interventional percutaneous placement of an irrigation drainage.
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy, history of organ transplantation, inability to administer antibiotics
